title: Ultra-High-Speed Rotor for Improved Characterization of Microparticle-Surface Adhesion
content: Microparticle-surface interaction is important across different fields such as pharmaceuticals, material science, nanotechnology, and environmental studies. These interactions influence dust control, paint bonding, drug delivery, action of cells, and the stability of nanoparticles directly. Multiple forces such as van der Waals interactions, electrostatic attractions, mechanical interlocking and capillary forces contribute to microparticle-surface adhesion [1]. There are challenges in understanding the principles of how these forces are involved in microparticle surface adhesion. Factors such as capillary forces, non-homogeneous surface chemistry, non-ideal surface geometry, and effects of residues or impurities determine which forces are involved in adhesion [2,3].
